My understanding was that in order to re-import resources that were exported either with:
a user-provided predicate that associates the target resource with others repository resources that are outside of the hierarchy of the target resource or
with the "inbound" flag that also associates repository resources that are outside of the target resource's hierarchy,
it is required to import the entire data directory that was exported, versus configuring the import to point at the target resource.

, Yes, that's my understanding.  If you import just the exported resource, you are likely not going to get all the resources exported (because the inbound triples are filtered out).  You may get placeholder resources created to make the links to those resources work, but the actual triples from that resource may not be loaded.

comments.body:
Sample exported resource RDF: https://gist.github.com/coblej/50d1be1d0fa18ea7d07581036352f9c2

Config file used for export:
https://gist.github.com/coblej/832c1b9b200e8614d84a84c63db73951

Config file used for import: https://gist.github.com/coblej/90d564115ed623a7fb718bab0c4ccae4

Imported object 

http://localhost:8984/rest/dev/14/70/13/e7/147013e7-8320-41cf-8e79-e5edd68e49d4 does not contain any of the following predicates: `ns004:local`, `ns003:isGovernedBy`, `ns001:hasModel`, `ns005:isMemberOfCollection`.  The `fedora:created` and `fedora:lastModified` dates are set to the import date.
Properties copied from screen for imported object: https://gist.github.com/coblej/5ada23a1f87cbe4f26b8b68a0a03ee34

My understanding was that in order to re-import resources that were exported either with:

  • a user-provided predicate that associates the target resource with others repository resources that are outside of the hierarchy of the target resource or
  • with the "inbound" flag that also associates repository resources that are outside of the target resource's hierarchy, 

it is required to import the entire data directory that was exported, versus configuring the import to point at the target resource.

Is that your understanding, Esmé Cowles?

Andrew Woods, Yes, that's my understanding.  If you import just the exported resource, you are likely not going to get all the resources exported (because the inbound triples are filtered out).  You may get placeholder resources created to make the links to those resources work, but the actual triples from that resource may not be loaded.
I'm closing this issue as part of a jira repository scrubbing. It appears to be out of date, no longer applicable, or addressed by future versions of Fedora.
